A 45-year-old homeless male presents with episodes of hemoptysis, generalized muscle pain, and
dyspnea. He acknowledges having experienced similar symptoms previously but did not seek medical
attention. Due to lack of regular medical care, his medical history is unknown. His vital signs show:
temperature 98.6°F (37.2°C), blood pressure 159/95 mmHg, heart rate 89/min, respiratory rate 28/min,
and oxygen saturation 90% on room air. Bilateral basilar crackles are noted on lung examination.
Laboratory findings are as follows: Serum: - Na+: 140 mEq/L - Cl-: 103 mEq/L - K+: 5.8 mEq/L -
HCO3-: 21 mEq/L - BUN: 33 mg/dL - Glucose: 129 mg/dL - Creatinine: 2.6 mg/dL Urinalysis: - Color:
Amber - Protein: Positive - Blood: Positive What is the most appropriate therapeutic approach for this
patient? Answer Choices: (A) Plasmapheresis monotherapy (B) Rituximab monotherapy (C)
Cyclophosphamide monotherapy (D) Methylprednisolone and plasmapheresis (E) Methylprednisolone
(F) Cyclophosphamide and rituximab (G) Intravenous immunoglobulin and methylprednisolone (H)
Prednisone and azathioprine (I) Methylprednisolone, plasmapheresis, and cyclophosphamide (J)
Methylprednisolone and cyclophosphamide
 A. Methylprednisolone, plasmapheresis, and cyclophosphamide
B. Rituximab monotherapy
C. Methylprednisolone
D. Plasmapheresis monotherapy
E. Methylprednisolone and plasmapheresis
F. Intravenous immunoglobulin and methylprednisolone
G. Cyclophosphamide monotherapy
H. Prednisone and azathioprine
I. Cyclophosphamide and rituximab
J. Methylprednisolone and cyclophosphamide
